symbols.name: Ddyad
symbols.def: signed dyadic rationals whose numerator and exponent have total binary encoding length at most \(L_n\)

symbols.name: Idy
symbols.role: deterministically certified interval from exact dyadic data

symbols.name: Deltaenc
symbols.role: certified propagation radius for observation encoding

symbols.name: Deltanum
symbols.role: total certified encoding and arithmetic padding radius

definitions.name: Strong-donor class \(\mathcal P_n\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_n=\{P=P_{A,u,v}:\operatorname{rank}(A)=r,\ cn\le s_r(A)\le s_1(A)\le C_0n,\ \max(\|U\|_{2,\infty},\|V\|_{2,\infty})\le\sqrt{\mu r/n},\ \max(\|A\|_{\max},\|u\|_\infty,\|v\|_\infty)\le B,\ u\in\operatorname{row}(A),\ v\in\operatorname{col}(A),\ \operatorname{vec}(E,e,f)\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2I_{n^2+2n}),\ 1\le r\le r_0\}\)

definitions.name: Donor-only rank-r truncated SVD
definitions.construction: \(X_r=\widehat U\widehat S\widehat V^{\top}\in\arg\min_{\operatorname{rank}(M)\le r}\|X-M\|_{\mathrm F}\), with a fixed measurable convention for singular subspaces

definitions.name: Donor-conditional reduced coordinates
definitions.construction: On \(G_n\), \(D_n=\widehat S^{-1}\), \(Z_{p,n}=(R\widehat V)^{\top}/\sigma\), \(Z_{q,n}=\widehat U^{\top}C/\sigma\), \(m_{p,n}=(u\widehat V)^{\top}/\sigma\), \(m_{q,n}=\widehat U^{\top}v/\sigma\), \(Z_n=(Z_{p,n}^{\top},Z_{q,n}^{\top})^{\top}\), \(m_n=(m_{p,n}^{\top},m_{q,n}^{\top})^{\top}\), and \(\xi_n=Z_n-m_n\)

definitions.name: Measurable observation encoding \(\mathsf{Enc}_{p_n,L_n}\)
definitions.construction: For \(y=(\operatorname{vec}(X)^{\top},R,C^{\top})^{\top}\), let \(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}=2^{L_n-p_n-\lceil\log_2(p_n+2)\rceil-4}\), \(\kappa_n=\mathbf 1\{\|y\|_\infty>T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\}\), and \(\operatorname{rnd}_{p_n}(x)=2^{-p_n}\operatorname{nint}_{\mathrm{even}}(2^{p_n}x)\), where \(\operatorname{nint}_{\mathrm{even}}\) is nearest-integer rounding with ties to an even integer. Set \((\widetilde X,\widetilde R,\widetilde C)\) coordinatewise to \(\operatorname{rnd}_{p_n}(y)\) when \(\kappa_n=0\), and to zero when \(\kappa_n=1\). Thus \(\mathsf{Enc}_{p_n,L_n}(X,R,C)=(\widetilde X,\widetilde R,\widetilde C,\kappa_n)\); on \(\kappa_n=0\), every coordinate error is at most \(2^{-p_n-1}\), and every encoded numerator and exponent has total binary length at most \(L_n\).

definitions.name: Exact-dyadic directed-rounding model \(\mathbb F_n^{\mathrm{dir}}\)
definitions.construction: The deterministic input consists of exact signed dyadic arrays \(\widetilde X,\widetilde R,\widetilde C\) and exact dyadic control values, or certified dyadic control intervals, with numerator and exponent bit length at most \(L_n\). Computation uses MPFR-equivalent radix-two arithmetic with a \(q_n\)-bit normalized significand, correctly rounded operations in both round-toward-minus-infinity and round-toward-plus-infinity modes, and an arbitrary-precision signed exponent. Overflow and subnormal values therefore do not occur in this abstract model. An IEEE 754 backend must instead apply certified exact power-of-two rescaling, widen its exponent range before endpoint emission whenever an overflow or subnormal flag is possible, and reject every flushed value. Bit cost counts \(n,L_n,p_n,q_n,\lceil\log_2(1/\alpha)\rceil\) and the bit lengths of all dynamically stored exponents.

definitions.name: Certified outward-arithmetic handle \(H_n^{\mathrm{cert}}\)
definitions.construction: Starting move: for exact dyadic \((\widetilde X,\widetilde R,\widetilde C)\), adaptively double \(q_n\) in \(\mathbb F_n^{\mathrm{dir}}\); use the coordinate boxes of radius \(2^{-p_n-1}\) about the dyadic arrays to propagate observation-encoding uncertainty through residual-certified enclosures of the retained singular values, invariant subspace, pseudoinverse, matrix products, and exact-real endpoints. Use a three-way accept--reject--uncertain spectral gate; the uncertain branch returns the outward hull of \([-M_0,M_0]\) and the certified on-gate enclosure. Enclose \(\Phi^{-1}(q)\) and \(F_{\chi^2_{2r}}^{-1}(q)\) in polynomial time by rational interval evaluation of the error and regularized incomplete-gamma functions followed by certified interval bisection or Newton steps until width at most \(2^{-q_n}\). Record the propagated encoding radius as \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\), all SVD, gate, quantile, scalar-function, and endpoint-rounding radii as \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}\), and return \(I_n^{\mathrm{dyad}}\) only with a containment certificate.

definitions.name: Composed encoded interval \(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}}\)
definitions.construction: Apply \(\mathsf{Enc}_{p_n,L_n}\) to the real Gaussian observations. Set \(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}}=I_n^{\mathrm{dyad}}\) when \(\kappa_n=0\), where \(I_n^{\mathrm{dyad}}\) is returned by \(H_n^{\mathrm{cert}}\) from the exact dyadic arrays and their coordinate-error boxes; set \(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}}=[-M_0,M_0]\) when \(\kappa_n=1\).

definitions.name: Certified numerical padding \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{num}}\)
definitions.construction: On \(\kappa_n=0\), \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{num}}=\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}\), where \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\) propagates the deterministic coordinate error \(2^{-p_n-1}\) from \(\mathsf{Enc}_{p_n,L_n}\), and \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}\) sums the nonnegative outward radii recorded by \(H_n^{\mathrm{cert}}\) for retained-SVD and pseudoinverse enclosure, gate classification, normal and chi-square quantiles, scalar calibration, and final endpoint rounding; on \(\kappa_n=1\), \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{num}}=M_0\).

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), conditional on \(X\) and on \(G_n\), \(Z_n=m_n+\xi_n\) with \(\xi_n\sim\mathcal N(0,I_{2r})\), \(\theta_{X,n}=\sigma^2m_{p,n}^{\top}D_nm_{q,n}\), \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}P(|\theta_{X,n}-\theta_n|>d_n,\,G_n)\le e^{-n/2}+3(e+n)^{-6}\), and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\mathbb E_P[d_n\mathbf 1\{G_n\}]/w_n\le K[\ell_n/\sqrt n+\ell_n^2/n]\to0\) for a fixed class-dependent \(K<\infty\).
statements.justification: This is the first changed proof step: it supplies the primitive experiment required by nonregular inversion without normalizing away the quadratic term.
statements.gap: Yan--Wainwright Appendix A retains the bilinear noise term but does not give this donor-measurable reduction with an expectation-compatible target-drift allowance.
statements.consumer: It makes first-order-degeneracy inference usable for CAST's four-block counterfactual subproblems.

statements.statement: For every invertible diagonal \(D_n\) and every \(m_n\in\mathbb R^{2r}\), the interval \([\sigma^2Z_{p,n}^{\top}D_nZ_{q,n}-\sigma^2W_n,\sigma^2Z_{p,n}^{\top}D_nZ_{q,n}+\sigma^2W_n]\) covers \(\sigma^2m_{p,n}^{\top}D_nm_{q,n}\) with probability at least \(1-\alpha\), has expected length at most \(K_\alpha\sigma^2(s(m_n)+\|D_n\|_{\mathrm{op}})\), and its length divided by \(2\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\sigma^2s(m_n)\) converges to one along every sequence with \(s(m_n)/\|D_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}\to\infty\).
statements.justification: A single analytic formula replaces nonlinear endpoint optimization while preserving exact finite-dimensional coverage and the regular Gaussian constant.
statements.gap: Bei--Navjeevan establish general minimum-distance validity, but not this explicit outer formula or its every-diverging-sequence length limit.
statements.consumer: Applied panel routines can evaluate the interval using one SVD and scalar special functions.

statements.statement: For the donor-only interval \(I_n^{\mathrm{out}}\), \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}P\{\theta_n\in I_n^{\mathrm{out}}\}\ge1-\alpha\), with no lower bound on either target loading. This strictly extends the loading-restricted Yan--Wainwright Gaussian interval by covering joint-zero and arbitrarily slow loading transitions in the same fixed-rank strong-donor model.
statements.justification: Uniform coverage across the degenerate cone is the central inferential claim.
statements.gap: Yan--Wainwright's main interval requires a loading-sensitive lower-bound condition, and their Appendix A does not construct an all-loading interval.
statements.consumer: CAST users obtain valid missing-mean uncertainty even when fitted target factor loadings are nearly zero.

statements.statement: There exists \(K_\alpha<\infty\), depending only on \(\alpha,c,C_0,\mu,B,r_0,\sigma\), such that for all sufficiently large \(n\), \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{out}})]/w_n\le K_\alpha\).
statements.justification: Coverage alone could be achieved by projection; transition-order expected length makes the interval informative at joint zero.
statements.gap: Neither the panel anchor nor generic minimum-distance theory proves a donor-uniform expected-length bound at the sum of first- and second-order scales.
statements.consumer: The bound supplies a principled uncertainty floor for entrywise treatment-effect reporting in strong-factor panels.

statements.statement: Along every sequence \(P_n\in\mathcal P_n\) with \(b_n/a_n\to0\), \(\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{out}})/[2\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)a_n]\to1\) in \(P_n\)-probability, without any prescribed rate at which \(a_n/b_n\) diverges.
statements.justification: Every-sequence adaptation rules out a hidden signal pretest that sacrifices slowly diverging regular sequences.
statements.gap: Bei--Navjeevan's general result allows a fixed conservativeness allowance away from degeneracy and suggests a tuning-based pretest; the panel literature has no exact all-sequence Gaussian-length constant.
statements.consumer: Regular high-loading counterfactual entries retain the same asymptotic length as the established Gaussian interval.

statements.statement: For every \(0<\delta<\min\{c,C_0-c,\mu-1,B\}\), every sequence \(P_n\in\mathcal P_n\) satisfying \((c+\delta)n\le s_r(A)\le s_1(A)\le(C_0-\delta)n\), \(\max\{\|U\|_{2,\infty},\|V\|_{2,\infty}\}\le\sqrt{(\mu-\delta)r/n}\), and \(\max\{\|A\|_{\max},\|u\|_\infty,\|v\|_\infty\}\le B-\delta\), and every measurable interval sequence \(J_n\) satisfying \(\liminf_n\inf_{Q\in\mathcal P_n}Q\{\theta_n(Q)\in J_n\}\ge1-\alpha\), there exists \(k_\alpha>0\) such that \(\liminf_n\sup_{Q\in\mathcal N_n(P_n)}\mathbb E_Q[\operatorname{length}(J_n)]/w_n(P_n)\ge k_\alpha\).
statements.justification: The converse certifies that the linear-plus-quadratic scale is intrinsic rather than an artifact of conservative inversion.
statements.gap: Yan--Wainwright's genie-aided lower bound targets the regular first-order variance and does not establish transition-width necessity at joint loading degeneracy.
statements.consumer: Methodologists comparing panel intervals receive an instance-local benchmark that projection or Bonferroni procedures can be measured against.

statements.statement: When \(r=1\) and \(b_n/a_n\to0\), the center and first-order half-width of \(I_n^{\mathrm{out}}\) reduce to the rank-one four-block spectral plug-in center and Gaussian variance formula of Yan--Wainwright, up to \(o_P(a_n)\).
statements.justification: The reduction is the required sanity check in the standard regular special case.
statements.gap: This is a compatibility result rather than a novelty claim; it prevents the transition construction from changing the established regular target.
statements.consumer: Existing rank-one implementations can adopt the transition correction without changing their regular-regime estimand.

statements.statement: For every exact dyadic triple \((\widetilde X,\widetilde R,\widetilde C)\) in \(\mathbb D_{L_n}^{n^2+2n}\), every real triple \((X,R,C)\) in its coordinate box of radius \(2^{-p_n-1}\), and exact dyadic controls or certified dyadic control intervals of length at most \(L_n\), there is a working precision \(q_n\) bounded by a polynomial in \(n,L_n,p_n,\lceil\log_2(1/\alpha)\rceil\) such that \(H_n^{\mathrm{cert}}\) terminates in bit complexity polynomial in the same quantities and returns \(I_n^{\mathrm{dyad}}\) containing the exact-real interval \(I_n^{\mathrm{out}}(X,R,C)\). The certificate gives \(0\le\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{dyad}})-\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{out}}(X,R,C))\le2(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}})\), remains valid for repeated retained singular values, computes outward enclosures of \(\Phi^{-1}\) and \(F_{\chi^2_{2r}}^{-1}\) in certified polynomial time, returns the bounded outward fallback hull whenever the spectral gate is uncertain, and never silently accepts overflow, a subnormal value, or flush-to-zero behavior.
statements.justification: This isolates the arithmetic obligation from probability by asking for a worst-case enclosure theorem on bounded exact dyadic data and explicit real preimage boxes.
statements.gap: Verified SVD results do not jointly certify pseudoinverse propagation, discontinuous gate logic, normal and chi-square quantiles, and exceptional floating-point states with polynomial bit complexity.
statements.consumer: Interval-library implementers obtain a deterministic certificate that can be audited independently of the panel sampling model.

statements.statement: Can one choose deterministic schedules \(p_n,L_n,q_n\), polynomially bounded in \(n\) and \(\lceil\log_2(1/\alpha)\rceil\), with \(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\ge B+\sigma\sqrt{12\log(e+n)}+1\), and compose \(\mathsf{Enc}_{p_n,L_n}\) with the deterministic dyadic certificate so that the resulting measurable interval \(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}}\), evaluated on the original real Gaussian blocks, satisfies \(\liminf_n\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}P\{\theta_n\in I_n^{\mathrm{fp}}\}\ge1-\alpha\), \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}P(\kappa_n=1)=o(n^{-1})\), \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_n]/w_n\to0\), and \(\limsup_n\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}})]/w_n\le K_\alpha\)? Along every sequence \(P_n\in\mathcal P_n\) with \(b_n/a_n\to0\), must \(\varepsilon_n/a_n\to0\) and \(\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}})/[2\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)a_n]\to1\) in \(P_n\)-probability? On \(\kappa_n=0\), the certificate must propagate the coordinate error \(2^{-p_n-1}\) into \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\) and satisfy \(I_n^{\mathrm{out}}(X,R,C)\subseteq I_n^{\mathrm{fp}}\) and \(0\le\varepsilon_n\le2\Delta_n^{\mathrm{num}}\); on \(\kappa_n=1\), it must return \([-M_0,M_0]\). Along every sequence \(P_n\in\mathcal P_n\) with \(r=1\) and \(u=v=0\), the \(P_n\)-expectation of each recorded summand of \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\) and \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}\), the fallback contribution \(M_0\mathbf 1\{\kappa_n=1\}\), and \(\varepsilon_n\) must be \(o(n^{-1})\).
statements.justification: This is the genuinely open statistical last-mile theorem: it must transfer a deterministic dyadic certificate to continuously distributed observations without changing the Gaussian model.
statements.gap: Panel papers assume exact operations, while verified numerics begins from finite encodings; no source supplies a measurable clipping-and-rounding interface whose propagated error is negligible in probability and expectation at the panel transition scale.
statements.consumer: A positive answer yields software whose reported CAST-style counterfactual intervals inherit coverage under the stated continuous Gaussian experiment rather than under an artificial dyadic-data model.

sampling_model.design: Four-block strong-factor panel experiment with one unobserved counterfactual mean and a donor-only spectral construction.
sampling_model.units: For each \(n\), the donor block is \(n\times n\), the target row is \(1\times n\), and the target column is \(n\times1\).
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment masks the lower-right untreated potential-outcome entry; identification of its mean follows from the exact rank and span restrictions.
sampling_model.overlap: No target-loading lower bound is imposed; donor singular values satisfy \(cn\le s_r(A)\le s_1(A)\le C_0n\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Known \(r\) and \(\sigma\); \(A\), its singular spaces, and both target loading coordinates are unknown and estimated only through the real Gaussian observations \(X,R,C\). The certified implementation first applies the measurable map \(\mathsf{Enc}_{p_n,L_n}\) and retains an explicit encoding-exception flag.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives Gaussian entrywise inference under condition \(4.4\mathrm{c}\); Appendix A retains a bilinear term after removing that loading lower bound.
Theorems 4.1--4.2 give uniformly valid minimum-distance inference for first-order-degenerate smooth transformations from a uniformly Gaussian primitive estimator.
Appendix C proposes a first-order bilinear interval and states that analogous validity requires modified projected-loading conditions.
Residuals from computed SVD factors produce verified enclosures for singular values.
Truncated SVD has explicit first- and second-order perturbation expansions and normwise remainder bounds.

tldr: A strong donor block identifies a missing untreated panel mean as \(\theta_n=uA^+v\), but the usual Gaussian interval loses uniform validity when both target loading projections approach zero. The donor-only interval \(I_n^{\mathrm{out}}\) retains the independent bilinear donor-noise term through an exact conditional Gaussian reduction, covers uniformly over fixed-rank strong-factor panels, has expected length of order \(w_n=a_n+b_n\), recovers the Gaussian oracle constant along every first-order-dominant sequence, and meets a local Kullback--Leibler length lower bound. The computational layer separates a deterministic directed-arithmetic theorem for bounded exact dyadic arrays from a measurable rounding map applied to the real Gaussian observations; the open transfer asks for polynomial bit complexity and encoding-plus-arithmetic padding that is uniformly negligible, including \(o(n^{-1})\) padding at rank-one joint zero.

project_justification.gap: Existing four-block panel intervals are sharp only after a target-loading lower bound, while generic first-order-degeneracy inference assumes that the primitive Gaussian experiment and its covariance are already available. Neither literature controls donor-SVD target drift at the quadratic \(n^{-1}\) width or certifies floating-point endpoints.
project_justification.niche: Known-rank Gaussian strong-donor panels isolate a finite-dimensional bilinear reduced experiment while retaining the repeated-spectrum, joint-zero, and arbitrarily slow-transition cases that defeat a single delta-method normalization.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the donor-conditional experiment, constructs an analytic outer interval with an observable donor allowance and bounded fallback, proves transition-order upper and lower length results, and separates the unresolved implementation into a deterministic exact-dyadic enclosure theorem and a measurable encoding transfer under the continuous Gaussian experiment.

related_work: Yan and Wainwright (2024) supply the identical four-block spectral estimator, regular Gaussian interval, and genie-aided lower-bound architecture; the present strict comparison is removal of their loading-sensitive interval condition while controlling length at the surviving bilinear scale. Bei and Navjeevan (2026) motivate minimum-distance inversion near a zero gradient and are used as an inference exemplar, not as a theorem-level target, because their results start from a uniformly Gaussian primitive estimator. Andrews and Mikusheva (2016) motivate nuisance-robust inversion under weak identification. Xia, Yan, and Wainwright (2025) make entrywise and bilinear counterfactual intervals operational for staggered adoption, but their Appendix C remains a first-order sketch with projected-loading conditions. Bordino, Berrett, and Klopp (2026) directly estimate multilayer bilinear forms and establish mean-squared-error bounds, but do not supply a confidence-interval or loading-degeneracy theorem. Bai and Ng (2021) establish the strong-factor tall-wide counterfactual tradition. Terao, Watanabe, and Ozaki (2025), Dopico and Moro (2004), and Vu, Chunikhina, and Raich (2021) inform the deterministic exact-dyadic SVD certificate but do not transfer it through a measurable encoding of continuous statistical observations. IEEE 754-2019 fixes directed-rounding semantics; the target additionally requires explicit rescaling, exceptional-state certificates, and outward special-function evaluation. Cattaneo, Feng, Palomba, and Titiunik (2025) provide a broader synthetic-control uncertainty benchmark without the strong-factor transition-length frontier.
technical_internal_limitation: The exact-real statistical interval and its analytic outer formula remain claims to prove. The unresolved numerical layer has two distinct obligations: a worst-case theorem for bounded exact dyadic arrays under directed arithmetic, and a statistical transfer after measurable rounding of the continuous Gaussian blocks. The latter must propagate coordinate encoding error, clipping probability, outward SVD and pseudoinverse errors, directed normal and chi-square quantiles, exponent growth, and spectral-gate uncertainty in both probability and expectation. Rank-one joint-zero loadings leave width of order \(n^{-1}\), so every encoding and arithmetic padding component must have expectation \(o(n^{-1})\); backward stability, an exact-dyadic assumption on Gaussian draws, or silent flush-to-zero behavior is insufficient.
honest_scope: The selected statistical kernel assumes known fixed rank, known homoskedastic Gaussian variance, square strong donor blocks, exact row and column span membership, and fixed incoherence and entry bounds. It does not claim unknown-rank adaptation, approximate-factor robustness, weak-donor inference, dependence robustness, or inference for a realized untreated outcome. In the regular rank-one special case it must reduce to the established Yan--Wainwright Gaussian formula. The observations remain continuously distributed Gaussian variables. The certified implementation applies a measurable finite-range dyadic encoding with an explicit exception flag, then invokes directed radix-two arithmetic on the encoded arrays; polynomial bit complexity, special-function enclosures, exceptional-state handling, negligible encoding transfer, and the rank-one joint-zero padding certificate remain explicitly open.

seed_details.title: General-rank transition-honest inference for one missing counterfactual mean
seed_details.anchor_location: Theorem 1, condition \(4.4\mathrm{c}\), Appendix A, Lemma 8, and the Discussion
seed_details.opportunity: Retain the bilinear donor-noise term before normalization and turn the resulting reduced experiment into one computable interval that remains valid when both target loadings vanish.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the normalization by the first-order variance in Yan--Wainwright with a donor-conditional Gaussian-coordinate reduction and inversion of the full linear-plus-bilinear functional.
seed_details.destination_search: Focused searches for missing-panel inference combined with vanishing loadings, quadratic degeneracy, transition length, and local Kullback--Leibler lower bounds found generic degeneracy inference but no complete panel theorem.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: An explicit donor-only truncated-SVD interval has uniform coverage, expected length within a fixed constant of \(w_n\), Gaussian-oracle length whenever \(b_n/a_n\to0\), and a matching local-neighborhood length lower bound for every fixed rank \(r\le r_0\).
seed_details.referee_objection: Immediate from Yan--Wainwright Appendix A and Bei--Navjeevan because the former retains the product term and the latter inverts degenerate transformations.
seed_details.rebuttal: The former supplies neither an all-loading interval nor transition-scale length, while the latter assumes an available uniformly Gaussian primitive experiment and does not control donor-SVD target drift at the \(n^{-1}\) floor.

seed_details.title: Coverage-preserving finite-precision spectral inference
seed_details.anchor_location: Sections 3.1--3.2 and the Conclusion on residual-certified singular-value enclosures
seed_details.opportunity: Integrate verified singular-value and subspace enclosures with the discontinuous rank cutoff and a bounded statistical fallback.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: First prove a deterministic enclosure theorem for bounded exact dyadic arrays under MPFR-equivalent directed radix-two semantics; then apply it after a measurable finite-range rounding map from the real Gaussian blocks and propagate the coordinate boxes into the endpoint certificate.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for certified SVD or pseudoinverse error propagation inside causal confidence intervals found numerical verification and panel inference in separate literatures only.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: A deterministic polynomial-bit-time directed-rounding certificate encloses every exact-real interval compatible with a bounded dyadic encoding box, and its composition with measurable rounding of the Gaussian observations adds expected length \(o(w_n)\) uniformly, including certified normal and chi-square quantiles, repeated retained singular values, an uncertain-gate fallback, and componentwise \(o(n^{-1})\) padding at rank-one joint zero.
seed_details.referee_objection: Routine from verified linear algebra because certified singular values and backward-error bounds already exist.
seed_details.rebuttal: Existing certificates do not connect bounded dyadic inputs to continuously distributed observations through a measurable encoding map, nor do they jointly propagate encoding error, directed special-function evaluation, overflow and subnormal safeguards, and a discontinuous statistical cutoff below the joint-zero width \(w_n\asymp n^{-1}\).

seed_details.title: Transition-honest inference for bilinear treatment-effect aggregates
seed_details.anchor_location: Section 3.3 and Appendix C, especially the paragraph following the proposed bilinear interval
seed_details.opportunity: Aggregate the four-block expansion before normalization so cancellation of projected unit and time loadings does not invalidate inference.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the Appendix C first-order Gaussian approximation by the full covariance-aware linear-plus-bilinear reduced experiment for the aggregate itself.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for staggered-adoption bilinear intervals with vanishing projected loadings found CAST's sketch and first-order linear-form results, but no transition-length theorem.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: A scalar interval for \(c_1^{\top}M_d c_2\) is uniformly valid under projected-loading cancellation and has aggregate first-plus-second-order length with a matching local lower bound.
seed_details.referee_objection: CAST Appendix C already states the bilinear confidence interval.
seed_details.rebuttal: Appendix C explicitly says an analogous theorem can be established only under modified projected-loading conditions and retains no quadratic transition scale or lower bound.

seed_details.title: Approximate-factor transition inference with a sharp residual-bias modulus
seed_details.anchor_location: Discussion, where extension from exact to approximately low-rank matrices is listed as open
seed_details.opportunity: Characterize the smallest worst-case missing-cell bias compatible with observed residual blocks and add it to the stochastic transition width.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Before the stochastic SVD expansion, derive an observable or sharp worst-case modulus linking the unobserved approximation residual to its observed blocks.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches located Choi--Kwon--Liao's approximate-factor central limit theory but no residual-bias modulus coupled to vanishing-loading second-order inference.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: For a named approximately low-rank class, honest length is equivalent to \(w_n\) plus a sharp extrapolation-bias modulus, with matching lower bounds.
seed_details.referee_objection: Immediate from approximate-factor inference by Choi--Kwon--Liao.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their first-order central limit theorem does not identify the missing residual's worst-case extrapolation bias or its interaction with the quadratic width.

seed_details.title: Rank-adaptive transition inference at spectral boundaries
seed_details.anchor_location: Algorithm 1 and Theorem 1, which take the rank as an input
seed_details.opportunity: Invert over rank-indexed reduced experiments and characterize the price of ambiguity near a donor spectral boundary.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace conditioning on a selected rank by a three-way spectral ambiguity guard before forming the pseudoinverse functional.
seed_details.destination_search: Choi--Kwon--Liao allow rank overestimation through diversified projections, while adaptive matrix-completion confidence sets address global norms; neither gives donor-entry transition length.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: An interval honest over \(r\le r_0\) recovers known-rank transition length on separated spectra and pays a lower-bound-certified ambiguity width at rank boundaries.
seed_details.referee_objection: Diversified projections already remove the need to estimate rank.
seed_details.rebuttal: They establish a first-order central limit theorem for linear functionals and correct ridge bias, not a loading-degenerate pseudoinverse interval or the rank-boundary length frontier.

seed_details.title: Simultaneous transition-honest confidence regions for a missing block
seed_details.anchor_location: Sections 3.1--3.3 on entrywise and bilinear inferential routines
seed_details.opportunity: Exploit the shared donor-noise quadratic form rather than Bonferroni aggregation of marginal transition intervals.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Lift the scalar conditional Gaussian reduction to the joint projected-coordinate experiment and retain its cross-entry covariance before taking maxima.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found simultaneous inference for noisy matrix completion and uniform post-treatment synthetic-control intervals, but not a joint first-order-degenerate donor-block law.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: A simultaneous band has honest familywise coverage and width governed by the Gaussian maximum plus a shared quadratic donor term, with a matching sparse local lower bound.
seed_details.referee_objection: A union bound over entrywise intervals immediately gives simultaneous validity.
seed_details.rebuttal: A union bound does not deliver the proposed covariance-adaptive width or a matching lower bound when many entries share the same low-dimensional donor perturbation.

seed_details.title: Unknown heteroskedastic noise through loading degeneracy
seed_details.anchor_location: Discussion and the variance construction in Appendix C
seed_details.opportunity: Studentize the reduced Gaussian-plus-quadratic experiment when row and column noise variances must be learned from donors.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the identity covariance of the projected loading coordinates by a donor-estimated covariance set before minimum-distance inversion.
seed_details.destination_search: CAST allows heteroskedastic first-order variance estimation, and Bei--Navjeevan assumes consistently estimated nondegenerate covariance; neither treats covariance estimation at the panel quadratic floor.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: A covariance-set inversion remains uniformly valid and transition-rate optimal with unknown bounded heteroskedastic variances.
seed_details.referee_objection: This is a routine plug-in covariance extension of the Gaussian result.
seed_details.rebuttal: At joint zero, covariance-estimation error acts on the leading quadratic law, so ordinary Slutsky arguments after first-order normalization do not apply uniformly.

seed_details.title: Joint donor-strength and loading-degeneracy phase diagram
seed_details.anchor_location: Discussion on improvability of the noise condition and dependence on rank
seed_details.opportunity: Let the least donor singular value move toward the noise spectral edge and characterize when the missing-entry functional remains inferable at nontrivial length.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the strong-factor subspace perturbation bound by a local spectral experiment before reducing target-loading uncertainty.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found weak-signal and spiked-matrix inference plus strong-donor panel completion, but no two-parameter frontier joining donor strength and target-loading degeneracy.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: A two-dimensional phase diagram gives necessary and sufficient scalings for honest finite-length inference and the minimax width in each donor-strength and loading regime.
seed_details.referee_objection: This is merely a spiked-matrix phase transition restated for a panel entry.
seed_details.rebuttal: The functional depends on two target projections and a pseudoinverse, so the inferential boundary is not the subspace-detection boundary and requires a distinct local experiment.

literature_map.anchor: Yan--Wainwright derive the four-block SVD estimator, a loading-restricted Gaussian interval, and an instance-wise lower bound; Appendix A retains the bilinear noise term without constructing a transition-honest interval.
adjacent_threads: Bei--Navjeevan establish minimum-distance confidence sets for first-order-degenerate smooth transformations once a uniformly Gaussian primitive estimator with well-behaved covariance is available.
Andrews--Mikusheva provide uniform conditional inference with functional nuisance parameters and motivate conservative inversion under weak identification.
Bai--Ng establish strong-factor tall-wide imputation and first-order normal theory for counterfactuals.
Bordino--Berrett--Klopp directly estimate multilayer bilinear forms and prove mean-squared-error bounds, but do not construct confidence intervals or analyze loading degeneracy.
literature_map.occupancy_verdict: No checked source combines donor-measurable transition coverage, constant-factor all-sequence length, a local Kullback--Leibler length lower bound, and certified computation for general fixed rank.

literature_map.anchor: Terao--Watanabe--Ozaki certify singular-value enclosures from computed SVD factors but do not address statistical coverage or cutoff uncertainty.
adjacent_threads: Dopico--Moro translate multiplicative backward stability into relative singular-value and singular-vector accuracy.
Vu--Chunikhina--Raich give first- and second-order perturbation expansions and remainder bounds for truncated SVD.
Ben-Michael--Feller frame the statistical last-mile gap between causal matrix-completion theory and practical use.
Yan--Wainwright's algorithm assumes exact mathematical SVD and pseudoinverse operations.
literature_map.occupancy_verdict: The numerical and statistical halves are adjacent but no checked theorem separates a polynomial-bit deterministic certificate on bounded dyadic arrays from a measurable encoding transfer for continuous Gaussian observations, excludes silent overflow or subnormal behavior, and budgets each encoding and arithmetic component below the rank-one joint-zero statistical width.

literature_map.anchor: Xia--Yan--Wainwright Appendix C writes a plug-in interval for \(c_1^{\top}M_d c_2\) and says an analogous theorem can be proved under projected-loading conditions.
adjacent_threads: Yan--Wainwright supply the scalar four-block expansion and genie-aided lower-bound architecture.
Bei--Navjeevan supply inversion tools for bilinear transformations near a zero gradient.
Cattaneo--Feng--Palomba--Titiunik give broad staggered-adoption prediction intervals and scalable optimization, without strong-factor transition-optimal length.
Xia--Yuan give first-order inference for linear forms under randomly missing noisy matrix completion.
literature_map.occupancy_verdict: The exact aggregate target is present, but its transition-honest theorem and aggregate lower bound remain unstated in the checked literature.

literature_checklist.author: Yuling Yan and Martin J. Wainwright
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorem 1 gives a loading-restricted Gaussian approximation, while Appendix A, Lemma 8 retains a bilinear term without an all-loading interval.

literature_checklist.author: Xinyue Bei and Manu Navjeevan
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorems 4.1--4.2 provide minimum-distance inference for first-order degeneracy conditional on a uniformly Gaussian primitive experiment.

literature_checklist.author: Eric Xia, Yuling Yan, and Martin J. Wainwright
literature_checklist.one_line: Appendix C proposes a bilinear plug-in interval and leaves its theorem to analogous analysis under projected-loading conditions.

literature_checklist.author: Isaiah Andrews and Anna Mikusheva
literature_checklist.one_line: Conditional tests attain uniformly correct asymptotic size in moment models with a functional nuisance parameter.

literature_checklist.author: Jushan Bai and Serena Ng
literature_checklist.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association
literature_checklist.one_line: Tall-wide strong-factor imputation yields counterfactual estimation rates and first-order normal theory.

literature_checklist.author: Trung Vu, Evgenia Chunikhina, and Raviv Raich
literature_checklist.one_line: Truncated SVD admits explicit first- and second-order perturbation expansions with remainder bounds controlled by the least retained singular value.

literature_checklist.author: Takeshi Terao, Yoshitaka Watanabe, and Katsuhisa Ozaki
literature_checklist.one_line: Computed SVD factors can generate verified enclosures for all singular values or the minimum singular value.

literature_checklist.author: Alberto Bordino, Thomas B. Berrett, and Olga Klopp
literature_checklist.one_line: Direct multilayer bilinear estimation has mean-squared-error upper and local minimax lower bounds, but no confidence-interval theorem.

literature_checklist.author: Matias D. Cattaneo, Yingjie Feng, Filippo Palomba, and Rocio Titiunik
literature_checklist.one_line: Staggered-adoption synthetic-control predictands receive nonasymptotic prediction intervals and uniform post-treatment inference.

literature_checklist.author: Froilan M. Dopico and Julio Moro
literature_checklist.venue: SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications
literature_checklist.one_line: Accurate SVD algorithms satisfy multiplicative backward-error bounds yielding relative singular-value accuracy.

novelty_justification: {"claim_boundary":"The proposal does not claim that quadratic inversion, product-normal inference, SVD perturbation, directed rounding, or the bilinear donor-noise term is new. The narrow contribution is their general-rank strong-donor panel transfer with all-sequence length and local-neighborhood lower bounds, plus the unresolved certified implementation transfer from continuous observations to bounded dyadic computation.","closest_results":"Yan--Wainwright (2024), Theorem 1 and Proposition 1, are the closest panel result; Bei--Navjeevan (2026), Theorems 4.1--4.2, are the closest nonregular-inference result.","new_object":"The focal object is the donor-only analytic outer interval \\(I_n^{\\mathrm{out}}\\), together with the transition scale \\(w_n=a_n+b_n\\), a deterministic directed-rounding envelope for bounded dyadic arrays, and its measurable encoding composition under the real Gaussian experiment.","strict_gap":"Yan--Wainwright normalize by a first-order loading-sensitive variance in their main interval, while their Appendix A stops at a three-term approximation. Bei--Navjeevan begin from a primitive Gaussian experiment and do not prove that a noisy donor SVD induces one with target drift negligible at the second-order panel scale. Existing verified-SVD work does not provide the measurable observation encoding, directed quantile, exceptional-state, discontinuous-gate, and \\(o(n^{-1})\\) encoding-plus-arithmetic padding certificate required by the panel target."}
